content.user_title: Operate GKE Clusters with Expert Guidance
content.value_statement: GKE operations can be complex across deployment, scaling, identity, and troubleshooting. This skill provides practical workflows, commands, and production patterns for reliable GKE management.
actual_capabilities: Provides GKE cluster creation workflows for Autopilot and Standard modes.
Outlines deployment, service exposure, and autoscaling steps.
Guides Workload Identity setup between Kubernetes and Google service accounts.
Lists troubleshooting checks for pods, services, resources, logs, and events.
Summarizes production patterns for ingress, disruption budgets, security context, and cost optimization.
limitations: Does not authenticate to Google Cloud or run commands for the user.
Does not replace environment-specific review before production changes.
Uses placeholder names that users must adapt to their clusters.
May not cover every GKE feature or organization policy.

use_cases.title: Launch a GKE workload
use_cases.description: Plan a cluster, deploy a container, expose a service, and verify the rollout.

use_cases.title: Troubleshoot Kubernetes failures
use_cases.description: Investigate pod, service, event, and resource issues with focused GKE checks.

use_cases.title: Improve GKE security and cost
use_cases.description: Apply Workload Identity, security contexts, autoscaling, and cost controls to a cluster.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Cluster Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me choose between GKE Autopilot and Standard for a small web service. Include the main commands and assumptions.

prompt_templates.title: Deploy and Expose an App
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a GKE deployment plan for my container image. Include resource limits, service exposure, and verification steps.

prompt_templates.title: Diagnose Production Issues
prompt_templates.prompt: Guide me through troubleshooting a GKE service with failing pods and no endpoints. Ask for missing context before recommending commands.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Secure GKE Platform
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my GKE production design for Workload Identity, ingress, autoscaling, disruption budgets, and cost controls.

output_examples.input: I need to deploy an API on GKE.
output: A cluster type recommendation based on workload requirements.
A deployment and service checklist with placeholders to replace.
Verification steps for rollout, endpoints, and load balancing.

output_examples.input: My pod is stuck in CrashLoopBackOff.
output: Event and resource checks to identify scheduling or memory issues.
Likely remediation paths based on the observed failure mode.

output_examples.input: I want to lower GKE costs for staging.
output: Recommendations for Autopilot, autoscaling, Spot VMs, and resource requests.
A review checklist for non-critical workloads.
Warnings about changes that may affect reliability.

best_practices: Confirm cluster type, environment, and risk before changing GKE resources.
Replace placeholders with reviewed project, cluster, namespace, and service names.
Use Workload Identity and least privilege instead of static credentials.
anti_patterns: Running copied commands against production without checking context and namespace.
Using broad cleanup commands without labels, backups, or rollback plans.
Skipping resource requests, limits, and autoscaling configuration.

faq.question: Does this skill run kubectl or gcloud commands?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and examples. Users decide which commands to run in their own environment.

faq.question: Can it help with GKE Autopilot and Standard clusters?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes decision points and workflows for both cluster modes.

faq.question: Does it cover Workload Identity?
faq.answer: Yes. It outlines service account linking and annotation steps for Workload Identity.

faq.question: Can it troubleshoot production incidents?
faq.answer: It can guide checks for pods, services, events, resources, and logs. Production actions still need operator approval.

faq.question: Does it replace official Google Cloud documentation?
faq.answer: No. It summarizes common workflows and points users to official documentation for deeper detail.

faq.question: Who is this skill for?
faq.answer: It is for platform engineers, DevOps teams, and SREs who manage GKE workloads.
